macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer sharp AI-led selloff
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.1%, while the S&P 500 dropped roughly 3.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined about 1.9%. The S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory, while the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains amid renewed concerns over AI-stock valuations and Anthropic’s disappointing market debut.

items.title: Nvidia and semiconductor shares plunge
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell about 14%, while Micron dropped 13.9% and AMD declined 13.3% as investors reduced exposure to chip and AI stocks. Reports of possible SEC scrutiny of Nvidia’s accounting practices added to selling pressure.

items.title: Fed official argues for further rate hikes
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the current policy rate is not sufficiently restrictive given inflation levels, signaling support for continued monetary tightening. The comments contributed to pressure on risk assets and weighed on expectations for easier policy.

items.title: U.S. consumer sentiment improves modestly
items.summary: The University of Michigan’s November consumer-sentiment reading was revised up to 51.5, its highest level in three months. The improvement came as markets remained focused on inflation, interest rates and the Federal Reserve’s next policy steps.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds after falling to two-year low
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped to $55,252, its lowest level since September 2024, before recovering to about $60,192—an intraday rebound of nearly 9%. The broader sell-off also drove roughly $2.09 billion in crypto-futures liquidations, with long positions accounting for most of the total.

items.title: XRP falls 9% as bullish futures positions unwind
items.summary: XRP traded near $0.87, about 9% below its level a day earlier. Approximately $18 million in XRP futures positions were liquidated, with long positions representing 94% of the total.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation reportedly sells 2,500 ETH
items.summary: On-chain records reportedly showed an Ethereum Foundation wallet selling 2,500 ETH for about $3.88 million while ether traded near $1,566. ETH later recovered to approximately $1,687.

items.title: Chainflip halts activity during Ethereum-vault investigation
items.summary: Chainflip paused swaps, deposits, and withdrawals while investigating a transfer out of one of its Ethereum vaults. The incident temporarily disrupted activity on the cross-chain platform.

items.title: Aave governance approves USAT borrowing on Avalanche
items.summary: Aave voters unanimously approved adding Anchorage Digital Bank’s USAT dollar stablecoin to Aave V4 on Avalanche. The approved configuration permits borrowing USAT but does not allow it to be used as collateral for another loan.

items.title: Hong Kong regulatory warning pressures HyperLiquid
items.summary: HyperLiquid’s HYPE token fell sharply amid broader market weakness and regulatory uncertainty. Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission had listed the platform as suspicious over allegations of unlicensed operations.

items.title: EU considers tighter oversight of non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: The European Union is reportedly preparing a 2027 review of MiCA that could bring stablecoin issuers based outside the bloc under more direct regulatory oversight.

items.title: Swift prepares tokenized-deposit blockchain pilots
items.summary: Swift said its blockchain ledger is ready for tokenized-deposit pilots involving 17 banks, focused on around-the-clock cross-border payments.

items.title: Bitdeer sells its entire weekly bitcoin production
items.summary: Bitdeer reported mining 281.1 BTC during the week ending November 20 and selling the same amount, up from 256.1 BTC mined and sold the previous week.

items.title: Sky Protocol’s USDS supply drops nearly 40%
items.summary: Sky Protocol’s USDS stablecoin supply reportedly fell by $2.07 billion, or nearly 40%, in 24 hours as users exchanged USDS for Circle’s USDC through the Peg Stability Module.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a lower-cost model positioned below its flagship Gemini 4 Carbon for coding, research, and document-heavy work. Reports place it among the leading models on independent evaluations, with a 1-million-token context window.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight 26.4-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3.4 billion active parameters. Its repeated middle-layer architecture is designed to improve reasoning while remaining small enough for local use on higher-memory laptops.

items.title: Tencent launches Hy4 multimodal model
items.summary: Tencent’s Hy4 is reported as a 770-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with native image input and a 1-million-token context window. It became available through Together AI, expanding access to Tencent’s latest open model family.

items.title: OpenAI reports stronger protection against reasoning extraction
items.summary: OpenAI said GPT-6.2 Astra reduced the success rate of attacks designed to extract hidden reasoning from 54% on GPT-6 Astra to 0.2%. The update highlights an intensifying focus on model security and adversarial distillation.

items.title: Anthropic prices IPO amid major AI-industry attention
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly priced its initial public offering at $83 per share and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The listing represents a major milestone for an AI company and underscores investor demand for frontier-model developers.

items.title: AI capability gains remain strongest on verifiable work
items.summary: An updated METR analysis found that AI performance continues to improve rapidly on tasks with clear, verifiable outcomes, while systems remain weaker on work requiring judgment. The results add nuance to claims about broad autonomous capability.

items.title: Researchers report computer-checked Riemann Hypothesis proof
items.summary: A researcher affiliated with Anthropic reportedly announced a proposed proof of the Riemann Hypothesis formalized in Lean, enabling machine checking. The claim remains a major mathematical development requiring scrutiny and independent verification.

items.title: OpenAI updates policies on training competing models
items.summary: New usage policies reportedly prohibit using OpenAI models or outputs to create training materials for competing models, including grading rubrics, reinforcement-learning environments, and data-sorting systems. The change reflects rising concern over model distillation and competitive misuse.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI sets entertainment launch record
items.summary: Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales during its first 24 hours, making it the biggest entertainment launch ever, according to the company.[4][7]

items.title: GTA VI dominates gaming industry attention
items.summary: The long-awaited open-world game launched after more than 13 years and has received strong early reactions, while analysts expect it to significantly boost publisher Take-Two Interactive and platform holder Sony.[4][9]

items.title: GTA VI leads The Game Awards 2026 nominations
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly received eight nominations for The Game Awards 2026. Forza Horizon 6 received two nominations, while Gears of War: E-Day received three.[3]

items.title: Xbox Game Pass announces its next wave of additions
items.summary: Microsoft’s November Game Pass lineup includes Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 on November 24, followed by The Outlast Trials and Hela: of Mice & Magic on December 1, alongside other announced additions.[3]

items.title: The Finals Grand Major announced for Stockholm
items.summary: The Finals Grand Major 2026 is scheduled to begin November 27 in Stockholm, marking a notable upcoming event in the competitive gaming calendar.[2]

items.title: Xenoblade Chronicles 3 receives version 3.0.0 update
items.summary: Nintendo released version 3.0.0 of Xenoblade Chronicles 3, with updated patch notes accompanying the launch.[8]

items.title: European Union digital fairness proposal draws games-industry reaction
items.summary: Industry groups have criticized the European Commission’s draft Digital Fairness Act, warning that its potential impact could fall particularly heavily on European companies.[8]

items.title: Console shipments reportedly fell sharply in the third quarter
items.summary: S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan data cited by GameIndustry reportedly showed console shipments down 36.5% year over year to 6.4 million units in the third quarter.[8]
